message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for North Carolina Avenue.

I have $726 in cash and a nearly complete pink monopoly. North Carolina Avenue is mortgaged for $150, so I will cap my bid at that amount to preserve liquidity.

Bidding $50 nets $100 cash after mortgaging. This blocks p4 from completing a PA+NC pair. Pacific Avenue is owned by p1, so neither player can finish the green monopoly without it.

I am currently on Pennsylvania Avenue, which p4 owns but has mortgaged. I am not paying rent right now.

The real risk is future rolls hitting Park Place or Boardwalk. Selling all twelve houses from my pink properties would raise about $600 in cash.

I will bid up to $150. That is the mortgage value of North Carolina Avenue, so I break even after mortgaging it back. A bid of $149 would net me one dollar profit instead.

p4 has $763 in cash. They could buy North Carolina cheap and complete a green pair. Pacific Avenue is mortgaged and owned by p1, who has only $29. p1 is cash poor but holds the dark blue monopoly, which is dangerous. I will bid the minimum raise to $50.

I will bid $50. North Carolina Avenue is unimproved, so mortgaging it immediately after purchase should be allowed.

Standard rules allow mortgaging a property immediately after purchase if it has no buildings. If the game requires waiting, spending $50 reduces cash to $676, which is still safe given the house sale buffer.

p1 landed on North Carolina Avenue and declined to buy it. They only have $29 in cash, so they cannot afford the $300 purchase price.
